correctness.rationale: Weak transitivity makes every pointed generated frame equal to the root and its at-most-two successors. Across pairs of these one-to-three-world frames, colors are determined up to equality by set partitions of at most six states. The complete standard-library checker enumerates 2/16/159 labeled frames, their 2/10/37 isomorphism representatives, and all 320315 representative-pair/color-partition cases, directly verifying that depth-3 and depth-4 signature equivalences coincide globally. Recursion then stabilizes at every depth. Finite-vocabulary characteristic formulas give a depth-3 normal form. A concrete no-proposition, three-world pair is depth-2 equivalent but separated by Diamond-cubed true. The actual checker from the packaged path passed.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A result on all weakly transitive frames with a class-uniform upper bound of three would cover this finding, but such a result is implausible without branching restrictions and was not identified. Formula-dependent filtration, finite-width completeness, and structural completeness do not imply a uniform depth-three syntactic normal form. The two-branch restriction gives the crucial three-point generated-submodel reduction.

value.rationale: The exact fixed modal depth threshold is a mathematically natural expressive-power invariant for bounded-branching weakly transitive frames and is uniform over infinite frames and unrestricted finite proposition vocabularies. Sharpness witnesses show depth three is necessary. The result is not a mere frame-count census or a reformulation of generic finite-model existence; it bounds arbitrarily nested formulas and creates a finite-rank normal form without asserting a formula-length complexity guarantee.
